what_this_is: n18 against n19, claim by claim, from recorded runs of committed code with clean trees (jev_provenance::census_of_every_claim).
change: n19 decides the rounding test in whole units of the last written place, allowing only a bound on the binary error of the scaled value; past what a double resolves, the stored number itself matches, a figure further off than any rounding plus that uncertainty differs, and anything between is not compared (relation beyond_double_precision). n18's fixed slack of eight epsilons exceeded one unit at 15 decimals.
long_figures_in_the_frames: Four claims are written to 16 or 17 decimals, each an exact copy of the stored double; all still match. None is written to 7-15 decimals.
metadata_provenance: Every finding over all 361 stored trades is identical to v2.
regression_tests: jev_numeric::tests::rounding_either_way_at_a_half_is_the_only_convention (review's two 15-decimal figures now differ) and jev_challenge::tests::a_truncation_is_true_only_where_it_also_rounds (review's ten-decimal truncation now keyed false) both fail on the n18 code (4fdf393) and pass at n19.
